Vote - Accept-Straight-to-FInalization -

R. Ast notes that the typo correction in col. ii, 2 is already noted at BL 9.91, as is a reading that is not recorded in the app. As far as col. ii, 10 is concerned: Wilcken proposed epistelloumen (= episteloumen) in APF 3. From the photo I found it difficult to discount this as a possibility.

P. Heilporn adds: One would want to be able to zoom in a bit more on this image, but I think it looks good enough. I can see a rather clear alpha (better than mu), a good upsilon in a V-shape, and the horizontal line of the tau. The only thing that has me worried is that I don't see any abbreviation mark (and the tau doesn't appear to be supralinear).

J. Sosin is inclined to accept, but add complete app, indicating Wilcken's suggestion, APF 3 (1906) 376: ἐπιστέλλουμεν̣ for which read ἐπιστέλουμεν; also Rea's at BL9.91; the include the entire BL 9 entry for this text. Also, clean up commentary to indicate authorship and remove 1st-person.

Vote - Defer - Ann's typo correction in col. ii, 2 is already noted in BL 9, as is a reading that is not recorded in the app. As far as col. ii, 10 is concerned: Wilcken proposed epistelloumen (= episteloumen) in APF 3. From the photo I found it difficult to discount this as a possibility.

I corrected a typographical error in col. 2, line 2 (καταμεμακηχέναι). I had worried over the reading in col. 2, line 10, for some time and took advantage of being in Geneva to check my emendation on the original. I gave references and explanation for my change in the commentary ad loc.

list.item: 10 Ann Hanson: The new reading was made directly on the papyrus both by me and by Paul Schubert. αὐτήν refers to the honestissima femina (Ulpianus=Dig. 25.4.10) at whose house the pregnant Petronilla was ordered to give birth, but apparently did not (col. 2.1, 4-5). The name of the hon. femina appeared in the previous col., and she is present in col. 2 only through pronouns (1, 4-5). On the praetor's edict De inspectione ventris, see U. WILCKEN, APF 3, 1906, esp. 374.
